subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & SLA language (latency measurement, exclusions)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs from today's call

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our discovery on performance and streaming: 

- Acme target: 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for standard text-generation requests (no attachments), measured server-side.
- Throughput: steady-state 100 req/s with bursts to 200 req/s for 15m.
- Concurrency: expected 50 concurrent in-session streams.
- Streaming: critical for product UX (client consumes tokens as they arrive).

Actions:
1) Can you confirm the percentiles and whether p99 matters for any paths?
2) Any exclusions we should be aware of (large input sizes, batch inference windows)?
3) I'll put together a draft SLO language and measurement approach for your review — linking an initial draft.

Attached: SLO-draft-v1.pdf (initial wording + measurement notes).

Thanks — happy to hop on another short call if helpful.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acme.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs from today's call

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming details from our side: 

- 95th percentile latency target: <= 250ms for typical user queries (text-only) is correct. We also care about p99 for admin dashboards (target <= 500ms).
- Throughput/Concurrency: 100 req/s steady, 200 req/s bursty for up to 15 minutes; concurrency up to 50 active streaming sessions.
- Streaming: yes, must support token streaming (chunked delivery). We will have some long-running prompt sessions but those are low-volume.
- Exclusions: requests with file attachments or >8k tokens should be excluded from the core SLO; we can propose separate guardrails for those.

We'll need explicit measurement definitions in the SLA (server-side measurement, what endpoints are included, and how we handle transient infra incidents). Procurement asked that we capture reporting cadence (weekly aggregated report + monthly executive summary) and remedies for missed SLOs.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Director, Platform Engineering — Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs from today's call

Thanks Alex — that's helpful. A few clarifications from our side on measurement approach (see attached SLO-draft-v1.pdf):

- Latency definition: server-side request processing time (time from request received by Redwood edge to final token emitted), measured per request; p95/p99 computed on requests that meet "standard request" criteria (text-only, <= 8k tokens).
- Streaming measurement: for streaming requests we measure time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and per-token delta for the first N tokens (configurable). For the SLA we typically commit on end-to-end p95 latency for non-streaming and TTFB p95 for streaming start.
- Exclusions: maintenance windows, customer-driven load tests, and requests exceeding configured token limits. We'll list exact exclusion definitions in the SLA.
- Reporting: we can provide weekly dashboards (token/req-level) and a monthly SLA report; we can also provide real-time alerts if SLOs breach.

I've attached an initial SLO wording and measurement section. Can you confirm: (a) that Acme is OK with server-side measurement and the exclusion list above; and (b) whether p99 for admin dashboards needs to be an SLA-ed metric or just an internal target?

If you confirm, I will loop in Legal (Rishi) and Security (Neha) to finalize SLA language and remedies.

Best,
—Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: Performance SLOs from today's call

Looping you both in to finalize the SLA language for Acme. Highlights from the thread:

- Customer wants p95 <= 250ms (text-only), p99 <= 500ms for admin paths (ask: do we SLA p99 or treat as internal target?)
- Streaming is required; propose SLA commitment on time-to-first-byte p95 and end-to-end p95 for non-streaming flows.
- Exclusions: maintenance windows, load tests, oversized requests (>8k tokens), and any customer-configured batch jobs.
- Reporting cadence: weekly dashboard + monthly SLA report.

Can you please: 
- Neha: confirm the exclusion language and whether our reporting cadence meets security/compliance needs (audit logs, retention).
- Rishi: propose remedies and credits wording (standard tiered credit approach vs. negotiated flat credit).

Thanks — aiming to send a proposed SLA excerpt back to Acme by 2026-07-28.

—Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & SLA language (latency measurement, exclusions)

Alex — thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise SLA excerpt that captures measurement definitions, exclusions, reporting cadence, and proposed remedies. Key points: 

- Measurement: Server-side processing latency measured at Redwood ingress to final token emission. Primary SLO: p95 <= 250ms for text-only requests (<= 8k tokens). Admin dashboard p99 <= 500ms is proposed as a non-financial target unless you want it elevated to a contractual SLA.
- Streaming: SLA commits to TTFB p95 <= 100ms and sustained per-token delta guarantees for interactive sessions; we include fallback routing in case of regional constraints.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (with 48h notice), customer-initiated load tests, malformed requests, and requests exceeding the configured token limit. 
- Reporting & Remedies: weekly dashboard + monthly SLA report; remedies follow a tiered credit schedule (5% credit for single monthly breach, 10% for repeated breaches within 3 months).

If this looks good, please confirm and we will: (1) route the SLA excerpt to Acme procurement and legal for review (DocuSign link included in related links for the draft), and (2) schedule a one-hour review with SRE next week to validate operational readiness.

Next steps requested from Acme: confirm whether admin p99 should be contractual and confirm acceptance of the listed exclusions.

Thanks — happy to adjust wording.

—Marissa
